objectives: Measure short /i/ sound recognition, decoding, spelling and comprehension separately.
Check whether short /i/ words are read accurately in isolation and controlled sentences.
Identify whether an error is primarily sound, decoding, encoding or comprehension related.
Use results to determine whether remediation or progression is appropriate.
concepts: Diagnostic checks should isolate component skills.
Accuracy comes before speed in early phonics fluency.

definitions.definition: An assessment used to identify strengths and specific learning needs.
Accurate, increasingly automatic reading of taught material.
Targeted instruction addressing an identified learning gap.

workedExamples: If sit is read as sat, check the middle vowel.
If pin is read as pan, check short /i/ decoding.
If words are accurate but a sentence question is missed, inspect comprehension separately.
commonMistakes: Treating all errors as the same.
Using a whole score without examining skill components.

basic: Complete short /i/ sound and word checks.
application: Read and spell taught CVC words.
higherOrderThinking: Choose the appropriate next step from an error pattern.
mixedReview: Combine decoding, encoding and comprehension checks.

mistakeBasedRevision: i/a confusion → vowel discrimination and encoding practice.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat the specific skill with minimal pairs before retesting.

outcomes: Learner demonstrates at least 80% accuracy on short /i/ recognition and decoding checks.
Learner demonstrates at least 80% accuracy on short /i/ spelling checks.
Learner answers controlled-text comprehension questions with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner uses accurate rereading to support developing fluency.
Teacher can identify the component skill requiring remediation.
